themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints spiked to 13 THIS WEEK—a 142% jump from the 5.4-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—signaling a possible coordinated dumping problem or enforcement gap in Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights.
evidence: 13 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.4-per-week 8-week average (z-score: 6.26, high severity)
Sustained focus on garbage/recycling infrastructure in community board budget requests suggests chronic sanitation issues
Timing coincides with potential seasonal transition or holiday waste generation
reporting_angles: Are specific blocks or industrial areas being targeted by illegal dumpers? Interview residents and DSNY.
Has enforcement or collection frequency changed recently? Check DSNY staffing and schedule changes.

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Piling Up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK—a 567% spike from the 0.8-per-week baseline—suggesting either a new bike-share abandonment pattern or lack of clearing.
evidence: 5 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8-per-week 8-week average (z-score: 6.43, high severity)
No prior news or social media discussion suggests this is under-reported in neighborhood discourse
Possible correlation with bike-share expansion or mechanical failures in the district
reporting_angles: Is this tied to Citi Bike or private bike abandonment? Map the complaint locations.
Has the city's abandoned bike removal process slowed? Check with DoT.

themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampments Up 7x
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 9 LAST WEEK—a 700% spike from the 1.1-per-week baseline—paired with repeated community board requests for homeless services, indicating an urgent unmet need.
evidence: 9 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1-per-week 8-week average (z-score: 5.78, high severity)
Community board has submitted repeated budget requests for homeless services (year-over-year pattern)
Panhandling complaints also up 2300% (3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 avg, z-score: 8.69), suggesting broader street homelessness crisis
reporting_angles: Interview unhoused residents and shelter operators: where are Bay Ridge's encampments forming and why?
Are DHS outreach teams active in the district? Have shelter bed allocations changed?

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints spiked to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 700% jump from the 0.6-per-week baseline—potentially indicating building code violations, aging infrastructure, or fire hazard risk.
evidence: 5 electrical complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6-per-week 8-week average (z-score: 6.29, high severity)
426 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (364 alterations) suggests active construction activity—may include electrical work
Asbestos complaints also spiked 700% (3 complaints 3 weeks ago), suggesting broader building safety issues
reporting_angles: Are these complaints concentrated in older residential buildings or commercial zones? Cross-reference with DOB violations.
Is this tied to the 9201 4th Ave and 9818 Fort Hamilton Parkway rezoning projects under ULURP review?

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street light complaints jumped to 29 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 150% spike from the 11.6-per-week baseline—compounded by rising encampment and panhandling reports, creating safety concerns.
evidence: 29 street light complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 11.6-per-week 8-week average (z-score: 4.38, high severity)
Converges with encampment spike (9 complaints last week) and panhandling spike (2300% up)—poor lighting enables street homelessness
May tie to maintenance backlogs or aging street light infrastructure in aging Brooklyn neighborhood
reporting_angles: Which streets/blocks are dark? Walk them and photograph. Interview residents about safety.
Has Con Edison or DOT cut maintenance staff? Check repair timelines on 311 complaints.
